title: CLEAN ECHOES
blurb: One part, one syllable. Only the tone moves.

families.origin: 青 is the colour of young plants: blue-green. On its own it is said qīng, and inside another character it passes that sound along. The radical beside it tells you what kind of thing is meant.
families.watch: The syllable holds but the tone moves: qīng, qíng, qǐng. A few cousins slid from q to j, as in 精 (jīng, essence) and 睛 (jīng, eyeball), and 猜 (cāi, to guess) has left the family altogether.
families.kin: 清请情晴蜻氰精睛猜

families.origin: 方 means square, and also a direction or a place. It is one of the busiest sound parts in Chinese: put it beside a radical and the character is almost always said fang.
ex: an action of the hand: letting something go
a bank of earth raised against a flood
families.watch: 方 can also be the radical. On the left of 旅 (lǚ, to travel), 族 (zú, clan) and 旗 (qí, flag) it began as a picture of a banner and says nothing about the sound. One true cousin drifted: 旁 (páng, side).
families.kin: 放房防访纺仿芳妨坊肪旁

families.origin: 马 is a horse, and one of the sixty radicals. It does two jobs. On the left of a character it is usually the radical and means horse. Elsewhere it is often there only for its sound, ma.
ex: a small spoken word that ends a question
families.watch: 骑 (qí, to ride) and 驾 (jià, to drive) are horse characters: there 马 is the radical and the sound comes from the other part. Always ask which part could be the meaning. In 驻 (zhù, to be stationed) the sound part is 主, the next family.
families.kin: 妈吗码骂玛蚂

families.origin: 主 began as a lamp with its flame: the thing at the centre of the room, and so the master or the main one. As a sound part it is one of the most dependable. Nearly every character built on it is said zhù, with a falling tone.
families.watch: 往 (wǎng, to go towards) looks like a member but is not: its right side was once a different shape that has worn down to look like 主. And 主 itself is zhǔ, third tone, while the family settled on the fourth.
decode: to be eaten by moths or worms
families.kin: 住注驻柱蛀拄

families.origin: 长 has two readings: cháng, long, and zhǎng, to grow. The family follows the second. All four characters below are zhang, and each one carries a different radical from the sixty.
families.watch: A sound part with two readings gives you two guesses. For 长 the first guess is zhang. Its other reading turns up only in rare characters such as 怅 (chàng, downcast).
decode: to rise, of water or prices
families.kin: 张帐胀账涨怅

title: A STRAY OR TWO
blurb: Dependable families, each with a member or two that wandered off.

families.origin: 巴 was a picture of a snake. Today it is mostly a sound: ba. It gave that sound to some of the first words a learner meets.
ex: what the hand takes hold of
a spoken word that softens a sentence
families.watch: The lips stay where they are but a puff of air is added: 爬 (pá, to climb) and 琶 (pá, in 琵琶 the lute) are said pa. 肥 (féi, fat) has wandered right away.
families.kin: 把吧爸疤芭笆靶爬琶肥

families.origin: 羊 is a sheep, horns and all, and one of the sixty radicals. It is also a sound part. Next to another radical it usually says yang.
ex: a small complaint of the skin
a gas, named for its sound
families.watch: Some members begin with x and keep the rhyme: 祥 (xiáng, good fortune), 详 (xiáng, detailed). And where 羊 is the meaning, as in 群 (qún, flock), it tells you nothing about the sound.
families.kin: 洋样养氧痒佯恙祥详翔

families.origin: 令 shows a person kneeling under a roof to take orders. Its sound, ling, rings through a large family, usually in the second or third tone.
ex: the neck, just under the head
the last light drops of a shower
families.watch: The l never leaves, but the rhyme can slip: 冷 (lěng, cold), 邻 (lín, neighbour), 怜 (lián, to pity). 命 (mìng, fate) is an old relative that kept the rhyme and lost the l.
families.kin: 领零龄铃岭玲伶羚聆冷邻怜拎

families.origin: 中 is a line through the centre of a target: middle, and the first half of 中国, China. As a sound part it says zhong.
ex: a heart that stays in the middle and does not sway
families.watch: 种 is also said zhòng when it means to plant. One relative took a puff of air: 冲 (chōng, to rush; to rinse).
decode: the middle one of three brothers
families.kin: 种钟忠肿仲衷盅冲

families.origin: 丁 is a nail seen from the side. It is said dīng, and two strokes are enough to carry that sound into a character.
ex: the very top of the head
families.watch: Three very common characters only half follow: 厅 (tīng, hall) keeps the rhyme, 灯 (dēng, lamp) keeps the d, and 打 (dǎ, to hit) keeps almost nothing.
families.kin: 顶订盯叮钉厅灯打

title: NEAR RHYMES
blurb: The rhyme holds while the first sound slides: b to p, g to h, j to x.

families.origin: 包 is something wrapped up, at first a baby in the womb. Its family splits in two: half say bao and half say pao. The lips are in the same place for both. The p only adds a puff of air.
ex: to hug, to hold in the arms
a skin of water around air
families.watch: You cannot tell bao from pao by looking. Guess the rhyme first, then try both. The tones wander as well: 雹 (báo, hail), 袍 (páo, robe).
families.kin: 饱抱胞苞雹鲍跑泡炮袍刨

families.mean: one of the eight trigrams; rare alone
families.origin: 艮 is rarely seen alone today. Long ago it showed an eye turned to look back. Inside a character it is a sound part with two voices, gen and hen, both made at the back of the mouth.
ex: the part of a tree below ground
the back of the foot, and walking behind
borrowed for its sound long ago
families.watch: The same part sits in 银 (yín, silver), 眼 (yǎn, eye) and 限 (xiàn, limit), where the sound has moved a long way. Outside gen and hen, do not lean on it.
decode: a scar, a mark left behind
families.kin: 根跟很恨狠痕恳垦银眼限

families.origin: 交 is a person with legs crossed: to cross, to meet, to hand over. Most of its family say jiao. A few changed j for x and say xiao, with the same rhyme.
ex: at first a part of a cart, later borrowed
once a wooden frame, then the place that keeps pupils in line
families.watch: 效 (xiào, effect) goes with 校. 咬 (yǎo, to bite) dropped the first sound altogether, though you can still hear the rhyme.
families.kin: 较饺郊胶狡绞跤校效咬

families.origin: 古 is ten 十 over a mouth 口: a story passed down through ten generations, so ancient. The family says gu, and a few members say ku or hu, all from the back of the mouth.
ex: a woman of the older generation
families.watch: 胡 (hú, beard; reckless) took the h and then became a sound part itself: 湖 (hú, lake), 糊 (hú, paste). 居 (jū, to dwell) has moved furthest.
families.kin: 故姑固估咕苦枯胡湖居

families.origin: 干 was a forked pole used as a weapon. Simplified Chinese uses it for two words, dry (gān) and to do (gàn). As a sound part it gives gan and, with a breathier start, han.
families.watch: 刊 (kān, to publish) starts with k, and 岸 (àn, shore) has lost the first sound entirely. The rhyme, an, is what lasts.
families.kin: 赶肝杆竿汗旱刊岸

title: WORN HINTS
blurb: Sound parts chosen two thousand years ago. Some have drifted a long way.

families.origin: 工 is a carpenter's square: work. When these characters were made, about two thousand years ago, they all rhymed with it. Speech has moved on since, and the family now spreads across gong, hong, kong and jiang.
ex: the Yangtze is the 长江
families.watch: The rhyme ong is the part worth guessing: 空 (kōng, empty) keeps it too. 江 (jiāng), 项 (xiàng, item) and 缸 (gāng, vat) show how far a sound can travel in two thousand years.
families.kin: 功攻贡红虹空江缸扛项

families.origin: 每 is a woman with her hair pinned up, borrowed long ago for the word every. Half its family still say mei. The other half kept only a trace.
families.watch: 海 is one of the commonest characters in Chinese and it does not sound like 每 at all. When a guess from the sound part fails, that is normal for an old family. 敏 (mǐn, quick) keeps only the m.
families.kin: 梅霉莓酶海悔敏侮

families.origin: 果 is a tree 木 with fruit on top. As a sound part it has two voices. Wrapped inside a character it says guo. Next to a radical it usually says ke.
ex: counting word for small round things
clothing 衣 split open with 果 wrapped inside
families.watch: g and k are made in the same place in the mouth, and that is all that links guo and ke today. 裸 (luǒ, naked) keeps the rhyme of guo and changes the start.
families.kin: 裹课棵颗稞窠裸

families.origin: 各 is a foot arriving at a doorway: each one, coming separately. Its family is split down the middle. One half says ge or ke. The other half begins with l: lu, luo.
families.watch: Linguists think the old word began with two sounds together, something like gl, and each half of the family kept one of them. A new character with 各 gives you two guesses, not one. 略 (lüè, brief) is on the l side.
families.kin: 格阁胳客路络洛骆略

families.origin: 分 is a knife 刀 splitting something in two 八: to divide. Its family holds to fen most of the time. The rest keep the lips together and change what follows: pen, pan, ban.
families.watch: f, p and b are all made with the lips, and that is the thread. 扮 (bàn, to dress up as), 颁 (bān, to award) and 贫 (pín, poor) each kept the lips and little else.
families.kin: 份粉芬纷吩氛盆盼扮颁贫
